post.summary: Apply a batch of content changes to a change request
post.description:
Applies an ordered array of content changes (up to 50) to the change request atomically, creating a single new revision. Changes are applied sequentially; if any single change is invalid the entire batch is rejected and no revision is created. Use this to create, update, rename, move, or delete pages within a change request before merging to live. This is the primary way to programmatically author content in a change request.
**Renaming a page** — `update_page` can change a page's `title` and/or its `slug` (the path segment used to build its URL within its current parent). Both fields are independent: to rename only the title without changing the URL, set `title` and omit `slug`; to change the URL without changing the title, set `slug` and omit `title`.
**Moving a page** — `update_page` can also change a page's parent and/or its position among siblings with `into`/`at`. Set `into` to the new parent's page ID, or `null` to move the page to the root of the tree; omit `into` to leave the parent unchanged. Set `at` to place the page at a specific zero-based index among its new siblings; omit it to leave the position unchanged (when the parent isn't changing) or append at the end (when it is). A page cannot be moved under itself or one of its own descendants. `insert_page`'s `into`/`at` remain the way to place a **new** page at creation time.
To put an image or attachment in a page, upload it with an `insert_files` change. Give the file a `ref` and a page inserted in the same batch can reference it as `![Alt](./<ref>)` or `[File](./<ref>)`, which resolves to the file's ID at apply time regardless of operation order. Uploaded files are also listed as `insertedFiles` when `compat=false`, and a file already in the change request can be referenced directly as `/files/<fileId>`. Inline `data:` URIs in markdown are not ingested and large image blocks are dropped, so upload the bytes with `insert_files` instead.
**Publishing an OpenAPI spec** — an OpenAPI spec belongs to the organization (see `createOpenAPISpec`) and appears in a space only through a page that renders it. Insert that page with an `insert_computed_page` change: `{ "operation": "insert_computed_page", "title": "API reference", "computed": { "type": "builtin:openapi", "props": { "models": true }, "dependencies": { "spec": { "ref": { "kind": "openapi", "spec": "<spec slug>" } } } } }`. GitBook replaces that page, at its position, with the API reference: one page per tag (or per operation with `"grouping": "by-operation"` in `props`), plus a models page when `models` is true, regenerated whenever the spec changes. Use `into` to nest the reference under an existing page. Do not recreate a spec with `insert_page`: `openapi-operation` blocks in a document only render the operations they name.
When page content is provided as markdown, links to other pages are resolved against the change request's current page tree. You can link a page by:
- Page ID — `/pages/<pageId>` (also `/pages/<pageId>#anchor`).
- Page slug path — `/pages/<slug>` for a top-level page, or `/pages/<parent-slug>/<slug>`
  for a nested page (e.g. `/pages/guides/getting-started`).

- Markdown file path — the path the page would have in Git: `/pages/<slug>.md` for a page,
  or `/pages/<slug>/README.md` for a page that has child pages. The space's root page is
  `/pages/README.md`.

- Relative markdown link — resolved against the page being edited, e.g. `./sibling.md`,
  `../other.md`, or `../README.md` (the parent page). Folder-style links without an
  extension (e.g. `./section`) resolve to that folder's page.

External URLs (`https://…`) are kept as-is. A link that does not match any page in the change request is left as plain text rather than causing the request to fail.
GitBook normalizes submitted content, so the stored page may differ from what was sent. To help callers reconcile local state with the stored result, the response can list each created and modified page with its resolved ID and a `urls.location` to fetch the page's persisted content.
For change requests with frequent concurrent edits, consider `expectedRevision` to protect against overwriting changes made since your read. If the branch has changed since the supplied revision, the batch is rejected with HTTP 409 and none of the submitted changes are applied.
**Response shape (`compat`)** — this endpoint is changing what it returns:
- `compat=true` (current default) returns the updated change request, matching the endpoint's
  original behavior.

- `compat=false` returns the updated change request **and** the list of affected pages (see
  the response schema).

The default is `true` for now to preserve backwards compatibility, but **will switch to `false` in a future release**, at which point the affected-page list is always included. You should pass `compat=false` if you want the new behavior today and avoid unexpected errors when the default flips in the future.

Classification of a site finding:
  - Outdated content: The content was correct but is no longer up to date with external context and may be misleading or incorrect.
  - Incorrect content: The content is factually wrong or misleading, leading users astray regardless of whether it was ever correct.
  - Content gap: The content is missing important information that should be present to answer user questions effectively.
  - Broken link: A URL on the site returns a 404, and can be resolved by creating a redirect or a new page.
  - Outbound link error: An external URL used by the site's content fails to resolve, and can be fixed by replacing or removing the link.
  - Other: Any other type of finding not covered by the above categories.

Where a link finding stands, from its status and what GitBook did with it.
  - `open` needs a fix.
  - `awaiting-approval` has a redirect GitBook drafted at its path, waiting to be approved or rejected.
  - `resolved` was fixed or closed: `servingRedirect` says whether a live redirect serves its path.
  - `ignored` was dismissed.

SiteFindingOrderBy.description: The field to sort site findings by. `updatedAt` returns the most recently updated findings first. `severity` returns the most severe findings first. `sources` returns the findings with the most linked sources (questions plus records) first. `suggestedFix` is for link findings: those that come with a fix (a suggested redirect, or an outbound link to correct) come before broken URLs the audit found no page for, most severe first within each group. Other finding types sort with the second group. Defaults to 'updatedAt'.

SiteFindingAutoResolution.description:
What GitBook did on its own to resolve a finding.
  - `drafted` drafted a fix that waits for approval.
  - `applied` has its fix live, applied on its own or approved from a draft, resolving the finding.
  - `undone` had its fix undone or rejected, so GitBook won't try again.

SiteFindingAction.description:
An action that moves a `broken-link` finding to another state. A finding's `actions` lists the ones it allows.
  - `approve` makes the redirect GitBook drafted live, which resolves the finding.
  - `reject` deletes the redirect GitBook drafted; the finding stays open and GitBook won't draft a fix for it again.
  - `create-redirect` creates a redirect for its path with `createSiteRedirect`, prefilled with the suggestion; it resolves the finding.
  - `mark-resolved` resolves it without a redirect: visitors still get a 404.
  - `reopen` reopens it, deleting the live redirect at its path. For a fix GitBook applied, this undoes the fix and GitBook won't fix the link again.
  - `ignore` dismisses it.
  - `restore` reopens a dismissed finding.

A section group — a container that nests sections (and other section
groups). Discriminated by `type: section-group`. Up to one level of nested
section groups is allowed.

Stable identifier for this section group, used as the Git Sync key.
Must be unique amongst all other section groups of the site. For
example: `section-group-product` or `section-group-1`.
You can nest section groups only one level deep. For example, `section-group-1` can have a child section group `section-group-1-1`, but `section-group-1-1` cannot have a child section group.

GitSyncSiteStructureSpace.description:
A space — a single content unit in the site's navigation tree. Discriminated
by `type: space`.

The space's content either lives in the synced repository at the directory
pointed to by `content.directory`, or does not inherit the site's repository
when `content.directory` is `null`. Hierarchy comes from where the space
appears in the YAML (under a section, a section group, or at the root), not
from an explicit parent reference.

The directory is read as one book — the Markdown files it holds become the
pages of the space.

key.description:
Stable identifier for this space, used as the Git Sync key. Must be
unique amongst all other spaces of the site. For example: `space-docs`
or `space-1`.

site or the section is visited without a space path. Exactly one space
among each set of siblings carries it.

Directory holding this space's content, resolved from the site's
project directory — `./guides` under a site rooted at `docs/`
reads `docs/guides`. A leading slash escapes to the repository
root instead, so `/guides` always reads `guides`. Parent-directory
segments (`..`) are rejected.
The space does not inherit the site's repository.

Spaces inside a section are listed inline under `children`; a section holds
nothing else — nest sections under a section group instead. A site with
sections must mark exactly one section with `default: true`, and cannot also
list spaces at the top level of its structure.

GitSyncSiteStructure.description:
Hierarchical structure of a site in a Git Sync YAML. Each entry is one of
four node types: a section group, a section, a space, or an external link.

A **space** is a leaf holding content, pointed at a repository directory. A
**section** gathers spaces behind one top-level navigation entry. A
**section group** gathers sections. An **external link** is a leaf that
navigates away from the site to an absolute HTTP(S) URL — it may sit at the
root or under a section group, but never inside a section, and only exists
in a site that also has at least one section. A site either uses sections
(optionally alongside external links) or lists its spaces at the top level,
never both.

```yaml
structure:
  - type: space
    key: space-guides
    title: Guides
    path: guides
    default: true
    content:
      directory: ./guides
  - type: space
    key: space-api
    title: API reference
    path: api
    content:
      directory: ./api
```

The same two spaces behind top-level navigation entries:

```yaml
structure:
  - type: section
    key: section-product
    title: Product
    path: product
    default: true
    children:
      - type: space
        key: space-guides
        title: Guides
        path: guides
        default: true
        content:
          directory: ./guides
  - type: section
    key: section-reference
    title: Reference
    path: reference
    children:
      - type: space
        key: space-api
        title: API reference
        path: api
        default: true
        content:
          directory: ./api
```

Rules checked on import — a violation fails the sync, naming the offending
node:

- Every `key` is unique across the file, whatever the node type. Git Sync
  recognises a node from one sync to the next by its key, so a reused key
  leaves two nodes indistinguishable.
- Each section marks exactly one of its spaces `default: true`, and a site
  without sections marks one among its top-level spaces. The default is the
  space that opens when the site or the section is visited without a space
  path of its own.
- A site declaring any section marks exactly one of those sections
  `default: true`, and lists no space at the top level: once a section
  exists, every space belongs inside one.
- Sections hold only spaces. Section groups hold only sections, nested
  section groups (one further level), or external links — nothing nests
  deeper than that.
- External links are only valid at the root or nested in a section group,
  never inside a section. A site containing an external link must use
  sections, with at least one section declared.
- Spaces pointed at the same `content.directory` declare the same
  `content.language`. One directory is read once, so it cannot produce two
  languages at the same time.

`all` sets no specific focus, which is the default. `read-only` reads, searches and comments without editing. `current-page` focuses on the page the user is on and its subpages. `modified-pages` focuses on the pages a change request has already touched.

backgroundAgents.description: The background agents this conversation has started, oldest first. Present on every state event so a client can render each one's live status against the tool call that started it.

consultOnly.description: Whether this conversation can only be read. Set on a transcript the agent produced on its own — an agent review — which is published for its requester to consult rather than to be continued: the client shows no composer and the agent refuses a message sent to it anyway.

AgentStreamState.description: Payload emitted by the agent with its current state.

AgentStreamRPC.description: Payload emitted by the agent is responding to a RPC call.

MergeRulesEvaluationContext.description: Context available when evaluating merge rules expressions.

reviews.description: The reviews posted on the change request.

actor.description: The user who is attempting to merge the change request.

LocalizedContentRef.description: Localized content reference, keyed by locale. Contains overrides for non-default languages only.

FeatureNotAvailableError.description:
The requested feature is not available on the organization's or site's current plan.
The operation was not performed. The `error.type` value `feature-not-available`
identifies this response; `error.upgrade` provides the requirements for upgrading.

schema.description:
`error.upgrade` identifies the unavailable feature, the minimum required
plan, and the URL of the relevant plan settings.

`error.upgrade.requiredPlanName` is the human-readable plan name, such as
"Pro", "Essential", or "Ultimate", suitable for display to users.
`error.upgrade.requiredPlan` is the internal plan identifier for
programmatic use, such as "pro_2024" or "premium".

The required plan describes feature availability, not a price quote.

`getOrganizationSubscription` (`GET /orgs/{organizationId}/subscription`)
provides the current plan and `canManageBilling`, which indicates whether
the caller can manage billing. Otherwise, an organization administrator
must perform the upgrade. Upgrades require billing permissions and approval
of any price or billing changes.

The original operation can be retried after the upgrade is complete.

type.description: Identifies the FeatureNotAvailableError response in the OpenAPI spec.

returnPreferenceApplied.description: Confirms that the requested minimal response preference was applied.
